A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same autoregressive causal-inference framework. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised, and added content.

before.justification: V1 reports original maze, chess-endgame, and semi-synthetic PeerRead experiments, including additional results in Appendices B-D.

after.justification: V3 reports original results for those environments and adds maze scaling, PeerRead sensitivity experiments, and IHDP treatment-effect evaluation.

M1.justification: Sequencification, the next-token likelihood objective, and Monte Carlo intervention estimators remain unchanged. Appendix E adds a feedforward embedding layer for continuous IHDP values, a limited input-processing adaptation. Expanded explanations of randomized topological ordering describe an existing procedure.

E1.justification: V3 adds IHDP, covering treatment-effect estimation with mixed numerical covariates and continuous outcomes. Maze evaluation adds queries conditioned on the starting row and environments with up to five spatial dimensions. V1's 6x6 red-versus-blue path scenario with a shifted exit distribution is removed; chess and PeerRead coverage remains.

E2.justification: V3 introduces a deep Q-learning offline RL comparator for maze queries; v1's 'offline' condition instead evaluated an AR model trained on policy-generated data. IHDP adds comparisons with NN, random forest, causal forest, and CRNET in Table 5. The chess MLP and PeerRead MLP/C-BERT comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The main maze experiment replaces randomized/optimal-policy mixtures with a fixed goal, distance-weighted starting positions, and an explicit stochastic movement policy. It evaluates exactly six moves and four-move prefix interventions, with revised model configurations and training budgets; dataset size changes from 50,000 per dataset to 10,000. PeerRead's stated buzziness definition adds 'embed'. IHDP introduces absolute/relative ATE-error evaluation on random train-test splits.

E4.justification: V3 adds controlled sensitivity studies of maze dimensionality and path length, PeerRead training-set size, and GPT model size. It removes the earlier maze policy-mixture analysis and 6x6 two-path case study. The right-versus-down Monte Carlo example is partly retained in Appendix B, and the chess distribution-shift experiment remains.

E5.justification: V3 first reports three-trial means and standard errors for DARCIE's PeerRead ATT estimates, adds uncertainty to training-size experiments, and reports IHDP means and standard errors across 30 random splits. The existing 1,000-repeat chess Monte Carlo reporting remains. Figure 10's caption says standard deviation while Appendix D says standard error, leaving its band definition ambiguous.

E6.justification: PeerRead Table 1 changes BERT's relative errors from 16/15/18% to 37/34/43%, and GPT's from 20/25/29% to 34/19/10%, reversing their ranking. These revised trial summaries accompany a changed reported buzziness definition, so they are not established same-setting gains or losses. V1's GPT point estimates also appear in v3 Table 3. New maze, sensitivity, and IHDP results substantially expand the evidence; IHDP ATE error is 0.1104 for DARCIE versus 0.1085 for causal forest. Chess Table 2 is unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 Section 3.1 explicitly introduces unconfoundedness and positivity assumptions, including the requirement that p(a,x,y) be positive for all triplets. V1 did not formally state these assumptions. The principal likelihood, adjustment, and Monte Carlo equations remain equivalent, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a unified AR model for causal queries involving complex confounders and sequential actions. V3 narrows the abstract's 'any DAG' wording to 'a large class of DAGs', emphasizes queries beyond standard RL, and strengthens the introduction's comparison with prior work to a claim that all prior methods require fixed-length covariates and actions.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations of randomized ordering as protection against overfitting, the flexibility gained by retaining later actions, and RL's failure on partial interventions because it optimizes a policy rather than modeling the remaining-action distribution. It interprets the new scaling and sensitivity results. Known-graph, observed-variable, and prefix limitations remain, with a new suggestion to impute unconfounded missing values using mask tokens.

D1.justification: V3 adds a project-code URL, clarifies BERT's final-token masking procedure, and documents the continuous-input embedding used for IHDP. Appendix A updates maze architecture, training, and hardware details, including the change from a 1080 Ti to a Tesla T4. Most chess and PeerRead training information is retained, although the PeerRead weight-decay selection rule is removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion expands substantially to longitudinal and continuous-treatment methods, including Frauen, Bica, Nie, and Zhu, and causal generative models from Xia and Rahman/Kocaoglu. Positioning now explicitly contrasts unified multi-query learning with componentwise generative modeling. References supporting possible non-prefix generation strategies are removed; publication-year updates to retained works are not substantive additions.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the introduction, methodological explanations, experimental narrative, and conclusion. Related work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, and the framework receives a more detailed subsection structure, including a dedicated randomized-ordering explanation. The broader-impact statement is removed and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: V3 changes the document template and typography, redraws and combines the maze/chess illustrations, and replaces the main maze displays with AR/RL violin plots and heatmaps. It adds scaling and training-size plots and new tables. The right-versus-down display is reduced and moved to the appendix; the original PeerRead causal diagram and 6x6 illustrations are removed.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens validation of the framework's claimed flexibility: v1 lacked a maze comparator, systematic scaling tests, and uncertainty for its main PeerRead estimates. The added comparisons, sensitivity studies, and IHDP evaluation make applicability and reliability easier to assess, while clearer exposition and a code link improve accessibility. These gains outweigh the removed maze case study and remaining reporting weaknesses: PeerRead's superiority language exceeds Table 1's support, and Figure 10 inconsistently labels its uncertainty bands.
